notes: DJI D-Log M drone clip, Nov 10 2026: snowy creek and evergreens rising to a sunlit golden peak under a pale blue sky. Log footage needs real contrast and color: the golden alpenglow is the featured hue, evergreens a little richer, sky a little bluer, snow kept white (no warm highlight tint). No people, so the skin guard is off so the golden light can glow. Nov 12 revision: the user saw the trees go black as the gold peak comes into view, so the curve's dark end is lifted (shadows about 3x brighter, true black kept) while the bright end is unchanged; gold +38% (was +35%) so the peak measures the same as before. Nov 12 revision 3 (replaces revision 2, whose shadow and highlight moves changed over time and squeezed the midtones, so all the browns shifted at 12 s): exposure_offsets undo only the camera's real exposure dip (about 0.1 in code value, 13-17 s, measured frame to frame), the same for every color; shadow_lift_keys lift only the darkest tones so the backlit trees stay at about the early forest's brightness, easing up to a little brighter as the peak comes in (Y 66 to 76); a fixed warm_highlights rule brings the washed-out sunlit peak (12.5-15 s) to the same gold as later. Gold gain 1.3 so the gold matches the approved version. The curve's shadow lift stays halved. Revision 3b: the washed-out peak (12.5-14 s) came out yellower (hue 83-87) than the settled gold (62-64); warm_highlights hue -150 turns clearly washed-out warm highlights toward orange, so the gold stays at hue 58-63 from start to finish. Revision 4: the user found the mountain 'wayyy too orange' with no visible tree detail. The warm-highlight rule had been easing every bright warm pixel, which flattened the texture (detail 30 vs 45 in the approved version) and the hue turn made it redder (58 vs 63). Now the rule runs only while the peak is washed out (strength_keys, 12.5-15.5 s) and gently (ceiling 0.80, color 3, hue -80); the even exposure offsets are gone because they brightened the peak too; gold gain back to the approved 1.38. From 16 s the mountain measures the same as the approved version; shadow_lift_keys re-solved so the trees still go 66 -> 76. Revision 5 (the user asked to grade the mountain area separately): the per-pixel warm-highlight rule is replaced by region_grade. While the camera washes the peak out (12.5-16 s), the sunlit peak (warm, bright, top of the picture, softened mask, sky and snow left out) gets an even exposure cut, more color and a hue turn toward orange, the same for every pixel in it, so its texture is kept. Keys measured from the raw peak against its settled look at 20-23 s (0.653, 0.056, hue 63). Revision 6: the user showed the aspen grove mid-frame looking faded every time the browns changed. The dark-tones lift added the same amount to R, G and B (gray) and compressed contrast (grove contrast 15 -> 7, color 0.017 -> 0.011). Replaced by forest_boost: a gain on the code values (like more exposure), only in the darker forest below the peak, solved so the grove holds brightness 82 from 14 s with its contrast (13-19) and color (0.017-0.021); evergreens get gain**1.5 (54-67, as before); the peak and sky are masked out. Revision 7: the user saw grain in the top left (the boosted, very dark tree) and a narrow tree with an unnaturally dark top. Backlit treetops are tinted warm, not green, so in the top band the forest mask now takes greens or dark things (below about 0.25). The boosted areas are denoised with vaguedenoiser (wavelet, within each frame) before the boost; hqdn3d left diagonal streaks in the foliage at any useful strength, and its temporal part smears moving trees. A dark taper on the boost (less gain for the darkest specks) also made streaks and was dropped. Sharpening halved for this clip (downscaled 4K is already sharp; sharpening made the boosted noise worse). Grain in the top-left tree: 23-54% less, at higher brightness. Revision 8: the user still found the grain very bad and preferred the trees darker and clean, and asked for no two-toned trees. Forest boost cut to 45% of what it was (at most x1.39, no extra for greens: grain grows with the boost), stronger denoise on the dark areas (vaguedenoiser threshold 4, applied even where the boost is small), sharpening 0.3, and no top-of-picture rule in the forest mask at all, so the boost depends only on how dark a pixel is and a tree can't come out two-toned.
